findings.description: All three A outputs invent symbol-aggregated tax-lot models with cost-basis stacking and term classification (A1: per-symbol TaxLot with LT/ST buckets; A2: event replay with FIFO matching; A3: fixed-point TaxAdjustedLot with wash-loss disallowance). None model the actual accrual-lifecycle architecture (Accrued/Allocated/Moved/Paid states) or reserve-summary band present in real code.

All three B outputs correctly identify the accrual-lifecycle model absent from EARS text: accrual band (6 columns, Sale ID/Lot ID/Jurisdiction/Tax Year/Amount/Lifecycle State, one row per accrual) and reserve-summary band (7 columns, Jurisdiction/Tax Year/Accrued/Moved/Paid/Outstanding/Shortfall, one row per (Jurisdiction, Tax Year)) as distinct typed ranges.

All three B outputs correctly identify nullable Amount field in accrual band (renders empty if applied_cents is None) and that all five reserve-summary columns are always present (never blank) — boundaries unspecified in EARS text.

The one-sentence EARS spec (SHEET-FORMULA-004) is underspecified: it does not name lifecycle states, reserve summary, Jurisdiction/Tax Year dimensions, or the accrual-key structure (Sale ID, Lot ID). A-side fills the gap by inventing symbol aggregation; B-side correctly reconstructs the actual accrual-lifecycle model. The architectures are fundamentally incompatible.
